Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

get carried away verb

also be carried away, get carried away by, be swept away (by a feeling), be transported, don’t get carried away, carried away with enthusiasm

classical

Cic. Sen. 83: efferor studiō patrēs vestrōs videndī (Lewis & Short), s.v. studium
Traupman 99: efferor (+ abl.)

efferor, efferrī, ēlātus sum

passive of efferō, with the ablative of the feeling

be carried away (by a feeling)

Lewis & Short s.v. efferō: “to be carried away, transported, hurried away” by passions and feelings. The feeling goes into the ablative: studiō, īrā, laetitiā efferrī.

Other words

  • efferrī (studiō) — get carried away (by eagerness)

    classical · Cic. Sen. 83 (Lewis & Short s.v. studium); Traupman 95; Traupman 287

    The passive of efferre, “to be carried out (of oneself)”, with the feeling in the ablative.

Examples

  • efferor studiō patrēs vestrōs videndī

    I am carried away with eagerness to see your fathersCic. Sen. 83 (Lewis & Short)

  • Nōlī studiō efferrī.

    Don’t get carried away with enthusiasm.Traupman 95

See also fly off the handle.
